It follows from asymmetry, so without that property the prompt's one link does not settle it.

notes: RBox contraction paired with history-replace-0010: removes the revision's ORIGINAL property, that 'was a vassal of' is asymmetric (the revision makes it symmetric). Every query becomes "I don't know", including the three propositional ones (strong Kleene). The instances are the revision's (William and Philip I; John and Philip II), now asking whether it follows that the lord was NOT a vassal of his own vassal: yes while asymmetry holds, undetermined after removal. Residual risk, recorded: the real-world answer is also "yes" (the French king never held a fief from the Duke), so a model may answer "yes" from history and not from the property; a "yes" is a route around the removal, never a sign it worked. Near and far unrelated queries are the revision's (near is exempt from Rule 7 under contraction).
